messages.body_plain:
I think that what's going on is that as.data.frame doesn't know how to handle an object of class "compareIC". Since the object is just a data frame with a funny name, I think you should be able to fix it with:
C <- compare(N,M0,nobs=length(d[,y]))
class(C) <- "data.frame"

If that doesn't work, Can you run
C <- compare(N,M0,nobs=length(d[,y]))
dput(C)

and send the output?

Noam and Vince,
Thanks for the suggestions. Took me a while to get back to this, but you pointed me in some useful directions. I came up with a solution which I'll describe at the bottom, but first I'll respond to your suggestions.

So, to remind, C is a comparison table of 2 models:
>C <- compare(N,M0,nobs=length(d[,y])) #C is of some strange S4 class called "compareIC".

Noam, your first suggestion didn't work, but the class() and attr() functions were useful later on:
>
>class(C)
[1] "compareIC"
attr(,"package")
[1] "rethinking"
>
>class(C) <- "data.frame"
>C
Object of class "data.frame"
Error in getDataPart(object) :
  Data part is undefined for general S4 object

Noam, I didn't quite understand your second suggestion:
C <- compare(N,M0,nobs=length(d[,y])); dput(C) #and then send the output
Mainly because I still (after looking a bit) don't understand what dput does, or how to "send the output". But that is likely a conversation for another thread, unless you're itching to elaborate.

Vince, str(C) returns:
Formal class 'compareIC' [package "rethinking"] with 1 slots
  ..@ output:'data.frame':    2 obs. of  7 variables:
  .. ..$ k     : int [1:2] 4 3
  .. ..$ AICc  : num [1:2] 5446 5494
  .. ...#etcetera, more columns below

Any suggestions on how to interpret this? It looks like there's a data frame in there somewhere, but C$k, for example, returns
Error in C$k : $ operator not defined for this S4 class.
Nice to know about str() though.

My solution:
So, here's what I came up with after looking at the help files for class() and attr(). Just in case anyone's interested.
>
>C2=unclass(C) ; C2 #I believe this strips the "compareIC" class from C and reassigns it to a generic S4 object. Thoughts?
<S4 Type Object>
attr(,"output")
       k     AICc ... (more columns)
M0  4    5446.423
N    3    5493.882
>
>DF=as.data.frame(attr(C2,"output")) #attr(C2,"output) extracts the data-frame-like part from the generic S4 object C2, and as.data.frame reclassifies it to a standard S3 object of class "data.frame".

If anyone wants to elaborate on what exactly it is that I'm doing here, or if there's a more efficient way to do it, feel free to chime in. But for my purposes, this works fine now.

Cheers,
Jens

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm running large monte carlo simulation over a grid of data and I have a bottle neck with a subroutine. I hoping perhaps there is a way use apply() to speed this up, but I've been unable to come up with anything yet.

In my simulation I'm trying to estimate an upper and lower bound for the chemical weathering flux (cflux) at each grid cell.

In a general sense, chemical weathering flux is calculated by multiplying denudation (denud) by a chemical depletion factor (cdf) - so:

cflux  = denud * cdf

In reality, for a given denud value, there is an interval of plausible cdf values that I want to sample from.

I apologize in advance for the poor quality of the code and comments that follow.

-- code follows --
#I simulate a set of denudation values for a single grid cell via another
#subroutine import them as the vector v.denud.
#Since I'm not including the other subroutine - I'll just generate some data.

n <- 100
v.denud <- round(runif ( n, 1, 100 ))

#For each denudation value there is a plausible range of CDF values.
#This range (q.025 - q.975) of values is held in d.cdf.
#Again - just generate some data.

denud <- seq ( 1, 100, 1 )
q.025 <- runif ( n, 0, 0.5 )
q.975 <- runif ( n, 0.5, 1 )
d.cdf <- as.data.frame ( cbind ( denud, q.025, q.975 ) )

#clean up unneeded objects
rm ( denud, q.025, q.975)

#For each element in v.denud I sample over the interval in d.cdf where v.denud[i] == d.cdf$denud.
#First, I preallocate a output v.cdf
v.cdf <- rep ( NA, n )

#Use a for loop to cycle through each element in the vector v.denud
for ( i in 1 :  length(v.denud) ) {

  #extract the lower end of the sampling interval for the ith element in v.denud
  lower <- d.cdf$q.025 [ which ( d.cdf$denud == v.denud[i]  ) ]

  #extract the upper end of the sampling interval in v.denud
  upper <- d.cdf$q.975[ which ( d.cdf$denud == v.denud[i] ) ]

  #Finally, simulate a single CDF value for the ith element in v.denud
  v.cdf[i] <- runif ( 1, lower, upper)
}

#Multiply Denudation by CDF to estimate chemical weathering flux
v.cflux <- v.denud * v.cdf

#extract quantiles for chemical weathering flux
quantile ( v.cflux, probs = c( 0.025, 0.50, 0.975 ) )

-- end code --

In my real code, the for() loop iterates over a vector of length 10000 which takes a few seconds to run. That speed is unacceptable given the grid sizes that I'm running this over. Is there anyway to speed this up?

Thanks!

-s

--
Scott Morford
PhD Candidate - Soil and Biogeochemistry
University of California Davis

Hi Scott,

I'm not quite sure what you're doing, so I apologize if I've misunderstood. But it seems like you have two data sources: a vector v.denud of values, and you wish to find the value of v.denud in d.cdf$denud, then grab that corresponding row's min and max to draw a uniform sample from, parameterized by these values.

If this is the case, you can do a single initial match(), and then use runif (which takes vectorized arguments) in one go, without any for loops for apply(). However, match() with return NA if it can't match, and it only grabs the first entry — your data must be "joinable" for it to work correctly. Here is an illustration:

 > match(c(10, 1), c(10, 10))
1 NA
> match(c(10, 1), c(0, 0))
NA NA

The for loop is slow here because it's doing a O(n) calculation every time you enter d.cdf$denud == v.denud[i]. This just means that for your n elements, the runtime complexity is limiting in n (in contrast to a constant, or n^2, etc). In fact, even just refactoring this so it's done once in a loop rather than twice (and removing unnecessary which statements — `[` knows how to handle vectors of logicals) drops the runtime from 20 seconds to 17 (repeated N=1e4 times).

So if I understand you correctly (and again, not sure I see the big picture of your problem), you could do something like:

v.denud.alt <- round(runif(n, 1, 100))
matchApproach <- function() {
  idx <- match(v.denud.alt, d.cdf$denud)
  lower <- d.cdf$q.025[idx]
  upper <- d.cdf$q.975[idx]
  return(runif(length(idx), lower, upper))
}

This runs in 0.8 seconds (repeated N=1e4 times) to the for loop's 20 seconds (via system.time()). I've set the seed before each approach and the results are consistent.

Vince

You can use try() to catch the error and use it to determine the next step in your code. The expression
x <- try(expr, silent = FALSE)

will assign x the value of the expression unless there is an error, which case x will be the error message.

I can't test this without your data file, but I think what you want to do is this:
sigma=try(solve(A), silent=TRUE)
if(class(sigma)="try-error") {
  derror[[r]] <- NA
} else {
  D.error=(det(sigma))^(1/nvers)
  derror[[r]] <- D.error}
}
